extracted_claim: The OpenGL graphics pipeline transforms 3D coordinates to 2D pixels. Stages: Vertex Shader (configurable) -> Geometry Shader (optional, configurable) -> Primitive Assembly -> Rasterization -> Fragment Shader (configurable) -> Alpha Test and Blending. In modern OpenGL, developers MUST provide at least a vertex and fragment shader.
implementation_relevance: HSE uses this pipeline. The vertex and fragment shaders in renderer.cpp follow this exact structure.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Renderer class manages shader compilation and pipeline configuration

document_reference: Hello Triangle chapter, Vertex input section
extracted_claim: OpenGL processes 3D coordinates only when they are in Normalized Device Coordinates (NDC) range [-1.0, 1.0] on all three axes. Coordinates outside this range are clipped. The y-axis points up in NDC (unlike screen coordinates where y points down). The viewport transform maps NDC to screen-space coordinates.
implementation_relevance: HSE vertex data must be in NDC range. The projection matrix transforms from view space to NDC.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Primitive stores vertices that get transformed to NDC by the projection matrix

document_reference: Hello Triangle chapter, Vertex input section
extracted_claim: VBOs store vertex data on GPU memory. Created with glGenBuffers, bound to GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, data uploaded with glBufferData. Usage hints: GL_STATIC_DRAW (set once, used many times), GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW (changed often, used many times), GL_STREAM_DRAW (set once, used few times). Sending data CPU->GPU is slow; send large batches at once.
implementation_relevance: HSE uses GL_STATIC_DRAW for vertex data. The VBO lifecycle in HSE follows this pattern.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Primitive has m_vbo for vertex data

document_reference: Hello Triangle chapter, Vertex Array Object section
extracted_claim: VAO stores vertex attribute configurations and associated VBO/EBO bindings. Core OpenGL REQUIRES a VAO to be bound for rendering. A VAO stores: glEnableVertexAttribArray/glDisableVertexAttribArray calls, glVertexAttribPointer configurations, and associated VBO/EBO bindings. Created with glGenVertexArrays, used by binding before draw calls.
implementation_relevance: HSE uses VAOs. The m_vao member in Primitive stores the vertex attribute configuration.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Primitive has m_vao. Core requirement for rendering.

document_reference: Hello Triangle chapter, Element Buffer Objects section
extracted_claim: EBOs store index data for indexed rendering. Instead of duplicating vertices for shared corners, store unique vertices and specify draw order via indices. Created with glGenBuffers, bound to GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER. Draw with glDrawElements instead of glDrawArrays. The VAO also stores EBO bindings.
implementation_relevance: HSE uses EBOs (m_ebo member). Indexed rendering reduces vertex duplication.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Primitive has m_ebo for index data

document_reference: Hello Triangle chapter, Vertex shader and Fragment shader sections
extracted_claim: Shader workflow: (1) Create shader with glCreateShader, (2) Attach source with glShaderSource, (3) Compile with glCompileShader, (4) Check errors with glGetShaderiv/glGetShaderInfoLog, (5) Create program with glCreateProgram, (6) Attach shaders with glAttachShader, (7) Link with glLinkProgram, (8) Check errors with glGetProgramiv/glGetProgramInfoLog, (9) Activate with glUseProgram, (10) Delete shader objects with glDeleteShader.
implementation_relevance: HSE Renderer class follows this exact workflow for shader management.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Renderer compiles and links shaders using this pattern

document_reference: Hello Triangle chapter, Linking Vertex Attributes section
extracted_claim: glVertexAttribPointer configures how OpenGL interprets vertex data: (1) attribute location, (2) size (number of components, e.g. 3 for vec3), (3) type (GL_FLOAT), (4) normalize (GL_FALSE for floats), (5) stride (bytes between consecutive vertices), (6) offset (pointer to first component). Must enable with glEnableVertexAttribArray.
implementation_relevance: HSE must configure vertex attributes for position, color, and UV data.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Primitive configures vertex attributes during setup

extracted_claim: Two main draw functions: glDrawArrays (draws vertices sequentially from buffer) and glDrawElements (draws using index buffer). Primitives: GL_TRIANGLES, GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, GL_TRIANGLE_FAN, GL_POINTS, GL_LINES, GL_LINE_STRIP. glDrawArrays(primitive, first, count). glDrawElements(primitive, count, type, indices).
implementation_relevance: HSE uses glDrawElements for indexed rendering of primitives.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE Renderer issues draw calls via glDrawElements
